title: Company Secretary (CS) India: Exam & Subject Roadmap
description: A detailed guide focused on the levels, subjects, exams, and passing criteria for the Company Secretary course in India, as prescribed by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI).

nodes.label: What is a Company Secretary?
nodes.description:
A Company Secretary (CS) in India is a senior strategic professional who is an expert in corporate laws, governance, and compliance. Recognized as a 'Key Managerial Personnel' (KMP) under the Companies Act, 2013, a CS is the conscience keeper of the company.

The primary job of a CS is to ensure that the company adheres to all applicable laws and regulations. They act as the chief advisor to the board of directors on best practices in corporate governance and are the vital link between the company, its board, shareholders, and regulatory authorities like the Registrar of Companies (ROC) and SEBI.

nodes.label: CSEET Subjects & Exam Structure
nodes.description:
The CS Executive Entrance Test (CSEET) is the first level and the mandatory qualifying exam for all students who wish to join the CS course after their 10+2 examinations. It is a single, computer-based test designed to assess the aptitude of aspiring students.

The exam consists of four papers:

  • Paper 1: Business Communication
  • Paper 2: Legal Aptitude & Logical Reasoning
  • Paper 3: Economic and Business Environment
  • Paper 4: Current Affairs & Presentation and Communication Skills (Viva Voce)

nodes.label: CSEET Passing Criteria (Cutoff)
nodes.description:
To pass the CSEET and become eligible for the CS Executive Programme, a candidate must meet two conditions simultaneously. This is the cutoff requirement set by ICSI.

A candidate must secure:

  • A minimum of 40% marks in each of the four individual papers.
  • AND an aggregate of 50% marks in all papers combined.

Failure to meet either of these conditions means the candidate will have to reappear for the exam.

nodes.label: Executive Programme: Module 1 Subjects
nodes.description:
After clearing CSEET, students register for the CS Executive Programme, the second level of the course. It is divided into two modules. The subjects in Module 1 build the core foundation of law and tax knowledge.

The four papers in Module 1 are:

  • Paper 1: Jurisprudence, Interpretation & General Laws (JIGL)
  • Paper 2: Company Law
  • Paper 3: Setting up of Business Entities and Closure (SBEC)
  • Paper 4: Tax Laws

nodes.label: Executive Programme: Module 2 Subjects
nodes.description:
Module 2 of the Executive Programme focuses on the financial and securities law aspects of corporate management. It provides the knowledge required for financial compliance and dealing with capital markets.

The three papers in Module 2 are:

  • Paper 5: Corporate & Management Accounting (CMA)
  • Paper 6: Securities Laws & Capital Markets (SLCM)
  • Paper 7: Economic, Business and Commercial Laws (EBCL)

nodes.label: Executive Programme: Passing Criteria
nodes.description:
The passing criteria for the CS Executive exam are applied on a per-module basis. A student can choose to appear for one or both modules in a single attempt.

To pass a module, a candidate must secure:

  • A minimum of 40% marks in each individual subject within that module.
  • AND an aggregate of 50% marks in all subjects of that module combined.

If a candidate appears for both modules simultaneously, they must achieve 50% in aggregate across all seven papers to pass.

nodes.label: Professional Programme: Module 1 Subjects
nodes.description:
The Professional Programme is the third and final level of the CS examination, testing expert-level knowledge in governance and advanced law. Module 1 focuses on strategic compliance and risk management.

The three papers in Module 1 are:

  • Paper 1: Governance, Risk Management, Compliances and Ethics
  • Paper 2: Advanced Tax Laws
  • Paper 3: Drafting, Pleadings and Appearances

nodes.label: Professional Programme: Module 2 & Elective Subjects
nodes.description:
Module 2 of the final level covers complex corporate actions and strategic management, including one elective paper that allows for specialization.

The papers in Module 2 are:

  • Paper 4: Secretarial Audit, Compliance Management and Due Diligence
  • Paper 5: Corporate Restructuring, Insolvency, Liquidation & Winding–up
  • Paper 6: Resolution of Corporate Disputes, Non-Compliances & Remedies
  • Paper 7 (Elective): Candidates must choose one from a list, including options like (i) Banking Law & Practice, (ii) Insurance Law & Practice, (iii) Intellectual Property Rights–Laws and Practices, and more.

nodes.label: Professional Programme: Passing Criteria
nodes.description:
The passing criteria for the CS Professional exam are identical to the Executive level and are applied on a per-module basis.

To pass a module, a candidate must secure:

  • A minimum of 40% marks in each individual subject within that module.
  • AND an aggregate of 50% marks in all subjects of that module combined.

Clearing both modules of the Professional Programme marks the completion of all theoretical examinations for the CS course.

nodes.label: Job Opportunities After Qualifying
nodes.description:
After passing the CS Professional Programme and completing the required practical training, a member is highly sought after for various roles in the corporate sector. The career paths can be broadly divided into two categories:

1. CS in Employment:

  • Compliance Officer/Manager: Ensuring the company adheres to all laws and regulations. This is a key role, especially in listed companies.
  • Company Secretary & Legal Head: In many companies, the CS also heads the legal department, managing contracts, litigation, and intellectual property.
  • Senior Management Roles: With experience, a CS can rise to positions like Chief Governance Officer or Managing Director.

2. CS in Practice (PCS):

  • A qualified CS can obtain a 'Certificate of Practice' from ICSI and start their own firm.
  • They can act as a Secretarial Auditor, provide advisory services on corporate law, assist in company incorporation, and represent clients before the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT).

nodes.label: Becoming a Member (ACS)
nodes.description: The final step in the journey, after clearing all exams and training, is to apply to the ICSI for membership. Upon successful application and payment of fees, you are admitted as an 'Associate Company Secretary' (ACS) and can officially use the CS designation.

nodes.label: Salary & Career Outlook
nodes.description:
The salary of a Company Secretary (CS) in India depends on experience, industry, company size, and location:

  • Entry-Level (0–2 years): ₹4–8 LPA, typically in corporate secretarial or compliance roles.
  • Mid-Level (3–7 years): ₹8–20 LPA, with responsibilities like corporate governance, regulatory compliance, and advisory.
  • Senior-Level / Manager / CS of a Company: ₹20–50 LPA+, especially in large corporates or MNCs.
  • Top Roles / Board-Level CS / Corporate Governance Head: ₹50 LPA+ in leading firms, with potential for higher compensation in multinational or high-revenue companies.

Disclaimer: Salaries vary based on company size, sector, location, individual skills, certifications, and negotiation. Figures above are indicative averages based on available data.
